description: CALL of a LANGUAGE SQL stored procedure actually EXECUTES its BEGIN...END body - parameters, control flow, loops - and returns the body's RETURN value. Previously the body's procedural statements were only logged and the call returned NULL, which is why each test here asserts a computed answer rather than that the call succeeded. Covers a no-parameter scalar return, a parameter used in the return, an IF selecting its branch both ways, a FOR loop accumulating, a DEFAULT parameter both defaulted and overridden, and a body whose SIDE EFFECT is visible afterwards. Converted 1:1 from scripting/SqlProcedureCallTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE add_two() RETURNS INTEGER LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN 1 + 1; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE double_it(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN x * 2; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE classify(n INTEGER) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN IF (n > 0) THEN RETURN 'pos'; ELSE RETURN 'neg'; END IF; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sum_to(n INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ DECLARE s INTEGER DEFAULT 0; BEGIN FOR i IN 1 TO n DO s := s + i; END FOR; RETURN s; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE greet(name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'World') RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN name; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE log_and_return(v INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO proc_log VALUES (:v); RETURN v; END $$
